claims.text: This dispute was filed by the DRIVER, and the payment state it asks to disturb has already moved: the payments ledger records refund_issued_sgd 5.00 with payment_status REFUNDED, and the trip record logs the interim reversal at 2026-10-06T00:31:40 — SGD 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling is party-relative and means the present state stands; it never means 'restore a charge'. A rider win here is a ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed 5.00 SGD, so if the driver's no-show case is not made out on this record, the fee stays refunded, the driver's claim fails, and the rider keeps the money.

The only artifact that answers whether the driver sent an in-app chat message before cancelling is the chat export, and the trip record's own derived contact block attributes both message_count and obligation_met to it (EV-CHAT-06062). That artifact is IMPAIRED, not clean: weight_multiplier 0.9, issue code SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (artifact schema 1.1.0 against the case's 1.2.0). Because POL-NS-23 requires a message AND a call, the message limb is a deciding fact on the driver's side, and under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in any ruling that depends on it cannot exceed 0.90 — the trip record's derived block is not a second, independent carrier, because it names EV-CHAT-06062 as the source of the count it reports.

A fraud flag of 1 is carried on a party profile in this case (EV-RPROF-06062, rider_profile.fraud_flags) — a field POL-GEN-22 uses only to raise the confidence an AI ruling needs, and which can never decide a trip (POL-GEN-01). The confidence required here is therefore 0.95 whatever the dispute value, and the driver's no-show case, resting on the impaired chat export at 0.9 (SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH), caps at 0.90. The driver's claim cannot be made out to the standard the policy sets, and no fact about this trip is established against the rider out of that shortfall.

The fact the driver must prove — whether he messaged and called the rider before cancelling — is the very fact POL-GEN-26 names as one not to be resolved by inference from impaired evidence, and the rider's filed answer denies receiving any message from the driver. The only artifacts that could settle that conflict are the impaired chat export (weight 0.9, SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH) and driver-side telemetry. If the panel cannot fix the fact to the 0.95 the fraud flag requires, the case goes to a human reviewer with the open question stated; an escalated fee is held rather than collected, so the rider is not made to carry the disputed 5.00 SGD in the meantime.

No rider-side artifact on this record speaks to the wait at all: the GPS trace carries no rider track (rider_track is empty) and the only trace in the case is the driver-device trace, so the wait and the non-appearance are established solely from the side of the record that takes the 5.00 SGD if the claim succeeds. Nothing third-party was attached for this trip either — EV-ADVIS-06062-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, and carries no fact, so no independent record corroborates the driver's narrative of the six minutes.

claims.text: The driver's arrival at the pickup is established on the record. The trip record carries an auto-arrival event at 2026-10-05T20:22:00+08:00, and the driver-device GPS trace at 100% coverage puts the nearest fix 3.24 m from the pickup point, reporting an accuracy of 4 m — inside the 25 m accuracy filter and far inside the 50 m arrival radius that applies to a STANDARD pickup zone. The arrival event is therefore corroborated by the trace, and the free wait validly began when it did.

The free wait elapsed before the driver cancelled. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 20:22:00 and expired at 20:27:00; the driver cancelled at 20:28:40, 400 s after arrival. Cancelling after the free wait is exactly what POL-NS-21 permits.

Both limbs of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 were met before the 20:28:40 cancellation. The trip record shows one in-app call placed by the driver at 20:24:30 (unanswered, rang 25 s), and the chat log shows two in-app messages sent by the driver at 20:22:20 and 20:25:30. I disclose that the chat artifact is IMPAIRED: weight 0.9, issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (artifact schema_version 1.1.0 against the case's 1.2.0), so the message limb rests on evidence below 1.0; the call limb rests on the complete trip record at weight 1.0.

The rider's statement that she 'never got any message from the driver' is contradicted by the chat artifact's own delivery and read receipts: MSG-06062-001 was delivered at 20:22:21 and read at 20:22:47, and MSG-06062-002 was delivered at 20:25:31 and read at 20:26:00 — both before the 20:28:40 cancellation. The rider had the driver's messages in hand and read them. That artifact is impaired (weight 0.9, SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH) and I put it no higher than that; the rider's denial is the assertion that should be scrutinised, not the driver's conduct.

The rider's profile carries rider_profile.fraud_flags of 1, so under POL-GEN-22 (and POL-NS-26 for this category) the AI ruling stands only at a confidence of 0.95. That bar is met: the decisive facts — arrival, the elapsed free wait, the in-app call and the 5.00 SGD fee — rest on the trip record, the GPS trace and the payments ledger, each carried at weight 1.0 with no issues. The flag never decides the trip; it fixes the confidence the record must reach, and the record reaches it.

The fee charged is the fee the policy sets. POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show cancellation fee at 5.00 SGD, the payments ledger records exactly 5.00 SGD charged with fee_matches_policy true and no other fare lines, and the fare breakdown gives driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd as 5.00 under the fee_share_to_driver of 1.00. There is no fee-amount discrepancy, so no POL-NS-22 referral arises; where the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged.

Outcome is party-relative here and the present state has already moved the money against the driver. The interim reversal at 2026-10-06T00:31:40 refunded the 5.00 SGD to the rider and withheld it from the driver, and the ledger shows payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.0. POL-GEN-03 defines NO_ACTION as the present state standing, which would leave the driver 5.00 SGD out of pocket for a trip the rules say he was entitled to be paid for. Because the fee was validly charged on this record, the ruling that makes the driver whole is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

No fact needed to decide this case is missing, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. Arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace, the free wait elapsed, contact was made before cancellation, and the fee charged equals the policy fee — every element POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-23 require. POL-NS-24's driver-no-show test is keyed to a scheduled pickup time and this on-demand trip has none; the clause has no trigger to operate on, and the driver arrived and waited beyond the free wait in any event. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06062-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but no no-show rule turns on traffic, so that absence carries nothing.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee is correctly charged on the platform record, but the record cannot be brought to the confidence this case requires, so it goes to a human reviewer and the 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver stays held — neither collected from the rider nor paid out to the driver — until that review.

What this record does show. The driver's auto-arrival at 2026-10-05 20:22:00 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: the nearest fix is 3.24 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 4 m, inside the 25 m accuracy filter and well inside the 50 m radius for a STANDARD zone (EV-TRIP-06062, EV-GPS-06062). This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so the 300 s free wait ran from 20:22:00 and expired at 20:27:00; the driver cancelled at 20:28:40, 400 s after arrival, which POL-NS-21 permits. The amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes (EV-FARE-06062, fee_matches_policy true), so no fee-amount referral arises on that clause.

Why the case escalates rather than decides. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have BOTH messaged and called before cancelling. The call is carried by the trip record (20:24:30, unanswered, weight 1.0). The two messages (20:22:20 and 20:25:30) are carried only by the chat export EV-CHAT-06062, which the pre-pass marks IMPAIRED at weight 0.9 with issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (artifact schema 1.1.0 against the case's 1.2.0); the trip record's message count and obligation_met flag are derived from that same export, so they are not an independent second carrier of the message fact. The rider's profile carries a fraud flag (EV-RPROF-06062, fraud_flags 1), so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the ruling needs a confidence of 0.95 whatever the value (5.00 SGD). The message limb caps confidence at 0.90, below that bar. The driver's case therefore cannot be made out to the standard the policy sets, and under POL-GEN-26 / POL-NS-26 the matter is escalated instead of ruled on.

Open question for the human reviewer. The rider's statement that she received no message is not borne out by the chat export's delivery and read receipts (MSG-06062-001 read 20:22:47, MSG-06062-002 read 20:26:00), but that export is the impaired artifact at issue; the reviewer should determine, on the older chat service's records, whether the driver's messages were in fact sent and delivered before 20:28:40.

On the parties' surviving claims: the driver's points that arrival is established, that the free wait elapsed, that the call was placed, and that the fee equals 5.00 SGD are accepted; his point that the record reaches 0.95 is rejected, because the message limb rests on the impaired chat export. The rider's points that the chat export is impaired and not independently corroborated, that the fraud flag sets a 0.95 bar, and that the shortfall is not made up by inference are accepted; the parties' competing 'no rider-side artifact' and 'POL-GEN-26 not engaged' claims were discarded by the referee for undisclosed impairment and are not relied on either way.

No referral is added: the fee is the policy's 5.00 SGD (no POL-NS-22 referral), POL-NS-24's goodwill credit has no trigger on an on-demand trip with no scheduled time and no failed contact, and no no_show_cancellations_30d count appears on the rider's profile to trigger POL-NS-25.

ruling.explanation:
This is the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-06062, filed by driver D-10033 against rider R-53280 after the platform reversed the fee to the rider and recovered it from the driver. Both of you get the same analysis.

Most of the driver's account is borne out on the record. The trip record and the driver-device GPS trace — both COMPLETE, weight 1.0 — put the driver at Block 45, Sims Drive at 20:22:00: the nearest fix is 3.24 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 4 m, inside the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so arrival is corroborated. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from arrival (20:22:00) and expired at 20:27:00; the driver cancelled at 20:28:40, 400 s after arrival, so the wait elapsed. The trip record shows an in-app call placed to the rider at 20:24:30 (unanswered), and the payments ledger shows exactly the 5.00 SGD fee the policy fixes (POL-NS-22, fee_matches_policy true), so no fee-amount referral arises.

The obstacle is the message limb of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23, which requires a chat message as well as a call before cancellation. The only artifact showing the two driver messages (sent 20:22:20 and 20:25:30) is the chat export EV-CHAT-06062, and it is impaired: weight 0.9, issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (its schema version 1.1.0 against the case's 1.2.0), disclosed under POL-GEN-02(1). The trip record's contact summary is not a second, independent carrier — it names EV-CHAT-06062 as the source of the count and the 'complete' flag it reports — so the deciding fact 'did the driver message the rider before cancelling' is carried at 0.9, not 1.0.

Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in any ruling resting on that fact cannot exceed 0.90. But the rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so POL-GEN-22 — and POL-NS-26 for this category — require a confidence of 0.95. This record cannot reach that bar, and a ruling below the bar is escalated. POL-GEN-26 names this very fact — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling — as one to be escalated, not inferred, where the evidence carrying it is impaired. The case therefore goes to a human reviewer with the disputed 5.00 SGD held, neither collected nor refunded, and no money moves now.

Two further points. First, the rider's statement that she received no message is contradicted by the chat artifact's own delivery and read receipts (MSG-06062-001 read at 20:22:47, MSG-06062-002 read at 20:26:00), but that artifact is the impaired one and cannot be leaned on to the 0.95 standard. Second, the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06062-01 (weight 0.0) carries no fact, and no no-show rule turns on traffic.

Party-relative note for the reviewer: had the bar been met, the driver's entitlement would be DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD (the money the reversal took from him); were the contact obligation found not made out, the present state would stand as NO_ACTION and the rider would keep the 5.00 SGD. The open question is whether, treating the impaired chat export together with the platform telemetry, the message limb of POL-NS-23 is made out.
